QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_20

question.text: How is the replacement cost in a delivery default penalty calculated?

answer.text: Comparison spot price minus Settlement Price, charged only when the comparison spot price exceeds the Settlement Price — with separate comparison-price definitions for agri and non-agri commodities
A fixed percentage of the contract value
The difference between futures and spot price

explanation.text: The Logic: Replacement cost equals the comparison spot price minus the Settlement Price, applied only when the comparison spot price is higher than the Settlement Price. For agri commodities, the comparison spot price is the average of the three highest last spot prices of the five succeeding days after the commodity pay-out date. For non-agri commodities, the comparison spot price is the higher of the last spot prices on the pay-out date and the following day. The Trap: It is not a fixed percentage, not the full spot price, and not the futures minus spot basis. The direction also matters — there is no replacement cost when the relevant spot price is at or below the Settlement Price. Note: The replacement cost compensates the non-defaulting buyer for having to source the commodity from the spot market at an unfavourable price.
